humanities_role_explanation: Items are numerical/analytical questions over U.S. Treasury Bulletins to proxy enterprise financial document workflows; no humanities competence is targeted and the historical documents merely serve as an enterprise-style corpus.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Scanned and digital-native PDF pages (tables, charts, figures) and parsed text; questions are text. Oracle PDF pages are given as images; 3% of questions require visual reasoning over charts.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Grounded Reasoning: document parsing, retrieval across ~89,000 pages, and quantitative analysis (e.g., OLS regression, inflation adjustment) yielding a numerical answer; agents use search, file and Python tools; temporal revision verification of revised statistics; a few chart-based visual questions.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to grounded reasoning over a single corpus (U.S. Treasury Bulletins) in an enterprise setting.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude Opus 4.6/4.5, GPT-5.4/5.1, Gemini 3.1 Pro/3 Pro, Sonnet, Haiku, GPT-5 Mini, Gemini 3 Flash; agents via Claude Agent SDK, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI.

quantitative_metrics.note: Exact-match correctness at 0.0% absolute relative error threshold, plus 0.1/1/5% thresholds; latency, tool calls, cost.

summary: OfficeQA Pro is a 133-question benchmark of numerical, multi-document grounded reasoning over a century of U.S. Treasury Bulletins (89,000 pages). It evaluates frontier LLMs and agents across prompt-only, web search, oracle page and full corpus settings, and ablates parsing, table representation, retrieval and test-time scaling.
key_findings: Frontier LLMs score <5% prompt-only and <12% with web search; best full-corpus agent (Claude Opus 4.6) reaches 48.1% with raw PDFs and 54.1% with Databricks parsed documents; best oracle parsed agent 66.9%. Parsing with ai_parse_document gives 16.1% average relative gain. Humans scored lower than agents on a 30-question subset.
facets_explanation: Authors wrote a seed set and scaled with annotation partners SuperAnnotate and Turing, with questions reviewed with USAFacts; a second and third annotator verified answers, and two rounds of agent-conflict QA corrected ground truth or disambiguated questions. Questions must have a single unambiguous answer. Annotators are described as data annotation partners and not specifically humanities-trained; domain_expert is the closest label. Answering requires corpus retrieval and often web data beyond the prompt.
results_explanation: Claude Opus 4.6 agent with oracle DBX Parsed reaches 66.92 correctness at 0.0% error threshold (Table 1); Opus 4.6 improves from 36.1% to 57.1% (+21.0pp) with parsed vs PDF oracle pages in the LLM baseline, the largest input gap reported. Human baseline on a 30-question subset (oracle pages): Human 51.1 vs agent 71.1/72.2 Parsed; the gap of -15 is human 51.1 minus best model 66.9 (rounded), although the human subset is a different question set. Scoring-threshold gaps (e.g., 17-24% at 5% tolerance vs under 3% at 0%) are also reported.

humanities_role.quote: Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on niche academic knowledge or closed-world tasks, OfficeQA Pro evaluates end-to-end real-world enterprise capabilities of agents across document-intensive workflows

evaluation_set_size.quote: Unless otherwise noted, all results are reported on OfficeQA Pro.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Prompt Only: LLMs answer with the question alone, and no documents, tools, or external context.

gold_source.quote: We authored an initial seed set of questions and answers and scaled dataset creation in collaboration with data annotation partners SuperAnnotate and Turing.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: The benchmark must test multi-step reasoning that extends beyond parametric knowledge and forces systems to navigate to the correct documents and sections

answer_multiplicity.quote: Each question in OfficeQA Pro has a single unambiguous answer, enabling deterministic evaluation via exact match.

plurality_treatment.quote: In case (2) the question was revised to remove ambiguity, and in case (3) the ground truth answer was corrected.

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: LLMs are presented with the oracle page(s) after pre-parsing the PDFs using Databricks’ ai_parse_document

reported_best_score.quote: The Claude Opus 4.6 agent achieves the highest overall score, reaching 66.9% accuracy.
